title: AWS Load Balancing & Auto Scaling: Quick Revision
summary: Quick revision notes on ALB, NLB and GWLB, target groups, health checks, listener rules, Auto Scaling groups, launch templates, scaling policies, cooldowns and multi-AZ scaling.

chapters.title: Choosing a Load Balancer: ALB, NLB, GWLB
points: ALB works at Layer 7 (HTTP/HTTPS/gRPC/WebSocket): routes by host, path, header, query string, and can authenticate with Cognito/OIDC
NLB works at Layer 4 (TCP/UDP/TLS): millions of requests per second, ultra-low latency, one static IP per AZ (Elastic IP optional), preserves client source IP
GWLB works at Layer 3 (GENEVE on port 6081): transparently sends traffic through fleets of third-party appliances (firewalls, IDS/IPS)
Comparison rows: ALB = smart routing for web apps; NLB = raw speed, static IPs, PrivateLink; GWLB = inline security appliances
Only ALB supports WAF and path/host rules; only NLB gives static/Elastic IPs; ALB IPs change, so use its DNS name, never hardcode IPs

chapters.title: Target Groups and Health Checks
points: A target group is the set of targets (instance, IP, Lambda for ALB, or ALB for NLB) a listener forwards to; a target can sit in several groups
Health check settings: protocol, path (e.g. /health), port, interval, timeout, healthy threshold, unhealthy threshold, success codes (default 200)
Unhealthy targets are removed from rotation, and traffic returns once they pass the healthy threshold again
If every target is unhealthy, the load balancer fails open and routes to all targets (the zonal failover behaviour)
Deregistration delay (default 300s) lets in-flight requests finish before a target is removed; lower it for short requests
Common mistake: a health check path that needs auth or returns 301/302 marks healthy apps unhealthy; also the target security group must allow the load balancer's security group

chapters.title: Listeners, Rules and Routing
points: A listener is a protocol and port the load balancer checks for connections (ALB: HTTP/HTTPS; NLB: TCP/UDP/TLS); HTTPS listeners need an ACM certificate
ALB rule = priority + conditions (host-header, path-pattern, http-header, query-string, source-ip) + action; lowest number is evaluated first, default rule last
Actions: forward (optionally weighted across target groups for canary/blue-green), redirect (e.g. HTTP 80 to HTTPS 443), fixed-response, authenticate-cognito/oidc
Example CLI: aws elbv2 create-rule --listener-arn <arn> --priority 10 --conditions Field=path-pattern,Values='/api/*' --actions Type=forward,TargetGroupArn=<arn>
Mistake: rule priorities must be unique, and with no default target group action, unmatched requests get a 503 or 404

chapters.title: Auto Scaling Groups and Launch Templates
points: A launch template defines what to launch: AMI, instance type, key pair, security groups, IAM instance profile, user data; it is versioned (use $Latest or $Default)
An ASG defines how many and where: min, desired, max capacity, subnets across AZs, launch template, and attached target groups
Set health check type to ELB (not the default EC2) so the ASG replaces instances that fail the load balancer's health check; set a health check grace period for boot time
Everyday commands: aws autoscaling create-auto-scaling-group, update-auto-scaling-group --desired-capacity, describe-auto-scaling-instances, start-instance-refresh for rolling AMI updates
Launch templates replace launch configurations, which are deprecated and cannot be edited; mixed instances policy with Spot needs a launch template

chapters.title: Scaling Policies, Cooldowns and Multi-AZ, Cheat Sheet
points: Target tracking: pick a metric and target (e.g. ASGAverageCPUUtilization = 50%, or ALBRequestCountPerTarget); ASG creates and manages the alarms, and scales out fast but in slowly; the usual best choice
Step scaling: CloudWatch alarm plus step adjustments by breach size (CPU 60-70% add 1, above 70% add 3); simple scaling waits for a cooldown after each action, so prefer step or target tracking
Cooldown (default 300s) blocks further simple-scaling actions until it ends; target tracking and step scaling use instance warmup instead so new instances are not counted in metrics before ready

Multi-AZ: spread subnets over at least 2 AZs; the ASG balances instances evenly and rebalances after an AZ failure or recovery; enable cross-zone load balancing (ALB on by default, NLB off by default)
Cheat sheet: ALB=L7 routing, NLB=L4 speed and static IP, GWLB=L3 appliances; health check type ELB; deregistration delay 300s; min <= desired <= max; track ALBRequestCountPerTarget for web traffic
